svg.aria-label: Tartan Dictionary — a journey to Scotland. A map of the lands north of the Roman empire tracing tartan from the domestication of sheep in Mesopotamia (c. 8000 BCE) and the Hami fragment of the Tarim (c. 1200 BCE), west along the Tartan Silk Road to Hallstatt (the La Tène check, c. 700 BCE), the Gerum cloak in Sweden (c. 300 BCE), and on to Scotland — the Oakbank Crannog on Loch Tay (500 BCE), then Vindolanda (c. CE 100) and Falkirk (the Falkirk check, c. CE 260).
